shared_elements: low-relief carving on a large stone block/monolith
sets of parallel curved ridges/lines (finger- or claw-like)
schematic zoomorphic element with a rounded projecting snout/head
rectilinear panels or bands of relief
justification: Both surfaces carry schematic low-relief carving in which sets of parallel curved ridges read as fingers or claws and a rounded snouted creature-head projects from the surface, which is a mildly specific correspondence in convention. But the depicted content otherwise diverges: A is dominated by a horizontal sequence of rectangular cartouche-like panels of sign-blocks running along the block, whereas B shows a vertical figure with a hand/arm gripping or flanking a bossed animal head, with no comparable band of repeated panels.
